item.title: Siemens Data Center Push Makes Skeleton Latest Baltic Unicorn
item.description: Estonia’s Skeleton Technologies has become the country’s latest tech unicorn after raising investment from Siemens AG to manufacture energy storage systems for AI data centers in the US.
item.dc:creator: Ott Tammik and Marilen Martin

item.title: Tech Leaders on Moving AI From Pilot to Scale
item.description: Mohamed Kande, Global Chairman, PwC; Kai-Fu Lee, Founder & CEO, 01.AI and Chairman, Sinovation Ventures; Pragya Misra, Head of Public Policy & Strategy, India, OpenAI; and Noboru Saito, President & CEO, TDK Corporation discuss what it takes to move enterprise AI from pilot projects to deployment at scale with Bloomberg’s Menaka Doshi at the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: MAIA: Interview of Guillaume Princen on Anthropic’s AI Strategy
item.description:
In an interview on October 14, 2026, Anthropic’s Head of International Startups & Digital Native, Guillaume Princen, discussed how startups and major firms are adopting Anthropic’s AI, including Claude tools, to boost employee productivity, overhaul processes, and build new products. He highlighted growing demand for frontier models like Opus 5.5, now about 40% cheaper than its predecessor, and a shift toward using different models for specific tasks across the 5.5 family. Princen emphasized Anthropic’s safety-first approach versus open-source and open-weight competitors, underscoring third-party auditing, closer cooperation with governments, and willingness to delay or limit powerful model releases—such as with Methos—if safety concerns arise, even at the expense of near-term revenue.
Original filename: 20261014_080546_Interview_of_Guillaume_Princen_on_Anthropic_s_AI_Strategy.mp4 (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Executive Says Open-Source AI Models Are Higher Risk
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s top sales executive outside the US argued that open alternatives to its AI models carry “more risk” of cybersecurity incidents or other dangers.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen and Tom Mackenzie

item.title: Ark's Wood Favors Nvidia, AMD in 'Volatile' Chip Cycle
item.description: Cathie Wood, founder, CEO and CIO of Ark Investment Management, discusses why she avoids traditional memory-chip players, saying the business cycle is "most volatile." Speaking on Bloomberg Television, Wood adds that we are "just at the beginning" of the artificial intelligence revolution. "In terms of our semiconductor exposure, [we] tend to be at the less-cyclical end of the spectrum," she adds. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sunil Mittal Warns AI Is Outpacing Regulation
item.description: Sunil Mittal says governments are struggling to keep pace with the rapid pace of AI innovation, and suggests that regulation should provide guardrails without stifling innovation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ASML Raises Full-Year Sales Outlook
item.description: ASML upgraded the low end of its 2026 sales forecast as increasing artificial intelligence spending boosts demand for the Dutch company’s chip-making machines. The firm projected annual sales of between €44 billion ($49 billion) and €45 billion this year. ASML's outlook offers an indication of investment plans by chipmakers like TSMC, Samsung Electronics and Intel. Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Billionaire Mittal Says OneWeb Leads Musk in India Satcom Race
item.description: Indian tycoon Sunil Bharti Mittal said his Eutelsat OneWeb venture is “significantly ahead” of Starlink in India’s satellite-communication approval queue, amid Elon Musk’s criticism that some oligarchs are blocking his attempts to gain spectrum access in the country.
item.dc:creator: Satviki Sanjay and P R Sanjai

item.title: India’s Goyal Calls US Ties ‘Very Good’ Despite Trade Tensions
item.description: India’s ties with the US are “very good,” Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said, even as trade tensions simmer and after President Donald Trump irritated New Delhi by claiming he helped mediate an end to armed clashes with Pakistan.
item.dc:creator: Anup Roy and Aryan Gupta

item.title: IMF, World Bank Tout Bangkok Blueprint Against Digital Fraud
item.description: The International Monetary Fund and World Bank unveiled a global roadmap to fight online financial fraud as increasingly sophisticated scams undermine confidence in digital finance.
item.dc:creator: Suttinee Yuvejwattana and Satid Sutipanya

item.title: ASML Rises as Chip-Gear Maker Can’t Keep Up With AI Demand
item.description: ASML Holding NV shares rose after the Dutch company said soaring artificial intelligence spending means it’s searching for ways to produce more chip-making machines over the next two years.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Jacob

item.title: Singapore’s PDG Seeks $1.2 Billion Loan for Malaysia Data Center
item.description: Asian data center operator Princeton Digital Group Ltd. is seeking a syndicated loan of up to $1.2 billion to fund its Malaysia buildout, according to a person familiar with the matter, as the debt binge to finance artificial intelligence infrastructure continues.
item.dc:creator: Kari Lindberg

item.title: Hitachi Energy CEO on AI, Energy Security and Grids
item.description: Hitachi Energy CEO Andreas Schierenbeck discusses whether the electricity infrastructure industry can expand fast enough to support the AI boom and industrial electrification, and how his company plans to convert demand into sustainable growth. He also explains why electricity networks are increasingly becoming a national security issue, not just an infrastructure challenge. He speaks with Shery Ahn from the sidelines of "Bloomberg New Economy Forum". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India’s Jaishankar on Key Foreign Policy Objectives
item.description: Dr. S. Jaishankar, Union Minister of External Affairs, Republic of India speaks with Bloomberg's John Micklethwait at the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Malaysia Taps China’s Satellite Tech for Earlier Flood Warnings
item.description: Malaysia is turning to Chinese satellite technology for earlier warnings of floods that hit the country during its annual northeast monsoon, Bernama reported.
item.dc:creator: Danial Azhar

item.title: China’s Producer Prices Jolted by Oil as Inflation Rebounds
item.description: China’s producer inflation swung higher last month, as escalating hostilities in the Middle East sent oil prices surging past $100 a barrel and goods related to AI became more expensive.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Why China Wants to Master the Robotic Hand
item.description: China is making a big bet on humanoid robots, with dexterous hands as its focus. It’s a key to building a stronger manufacturing base while addressing a slowly shrinking workforce. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China's Robotic Hands Key to $5 Trillion AI Humanoid Development Race
item.description: Advanced humanoid hardware is one of the strategic high-tech fields where China has an early lead over the US.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: OpenAI Says Staffer Arrested for Hidden Recording Device in Office
item.description: An employee at OpenAI was arrested and charged with using a hidden recording device in one of the company’s San Francisco offices, according to statements from the artificial intelligence company and the US Justice Department.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz and Samantha Oltman

item.title: A $90 Million Spyware Hack Sparks Review of Crypto Wallet Sales
item.description: Crypto hardware maker Ledger SAS is reviewing its policies and processes for how its devices are sold to consumers, after spyware implanted in some wallets led to an estimated $90 million in stolen cryptocurrency.
item.dc:creator: Emily Nicolle
